string.text: Developed in the 1980s by GLOCK for the Austrian army. Despite lacking any prior experience in small arms development, the gun was not only successful, it also served as a great example of proper implementation of polymers in modern firearms. Most of the frame is made of heat-resistant plastic, thus making the gun light but highly durable. Good ergonomics, reliability, and lack of traditional safety mechanisms (the user is able to fire immediately without separately manipulating a safety) all played their part in it becoming one of the most widespread civilian firearms for self-defense worldwide. A number of guns seem to have made their way into the Zone as part of standard mercenary equipment.
